title: Bug: empty --socket string gives truncated error message
description:
When --socket '' is passed (empty string), muxxy passes it to tmux_interface which tries to connect to an empty path. The error message is:

    tmux capture-pane failed for pane '%6': no server running on

The message is truncated after 'on' because the socket path is empty. This is confusing — the user sees a partial error message without understanding why.

**Expected**: either reject empty --socket at argument parsing time, or show a clearer error like 'no server running on empty socket path'.

**Impact**: low, but confusing for users who accidentally pass an empty string.
close_reason: Closed

title: Bug: custom --prompt regex set must cover all prompt styles to avoid timeout
description:
When using custom --prompt regexes (instead of --kind) for a REPL that can change prompt styles (e.g., SBCL dropping into debugger, or Python showing continuation prompts), the prompt set must include regexes for ALL prompt styles the REPL may show. If a command triggers a prompt style transition (e.g., exiting the SBCL debugger changes from '0]' to '* '), the new prompt won't be recognized and execute-command will time out waiting for idle.

**Example**: using only --prompt '^ *[0-9]+(\[[0-9]+\]|\])' for SBCL debugger prompts, then executing restart '1' to exit to top level — the final '* ' prompt is not matched, so wait_for_idle times out.

**Fix**: always include all prompt styles:
    muxxy --prompt '^\* ' --prompt '^ *[0-9]+(\[[0-9]+\]|\])' execute-command ...

**Impact**: this is a footgun for users who specify custom prompts. The --kind presets handle this correctly (they include all prompt styles), but the danger isn't documented.

**Reproduction**: see muxxy-31q for the specific SBCL case.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Daniel Jay Haskin
comments.text: Documented custom prompt-set requirement in README and agent skill: include every prompt style, with SBCL top-level/debugger example.

title: Bug: (abort) does not exit SBCL debugger — use numbered restart instead
description:
When muxxy drops into the SBCL debugger at prompt '0]' (or '0[2]' for nested), executing (abort) via execute-command does NOT exit the debugger to top level. The prompt stays at '0]' with the same restarts available. This is because SBCL evaluates (abort) in the debugger's own evaluation context, which invokes the ABORT restart of the evaluation, not the ABORT restart of the signaled condition.

**Workaround**: use the numbered restart (e.g. '1' or '4' for 'Exit debugger, returning to top level') instead:

    muxxy --kind sbcl execute-command '1' --timeout 10

**Canonical form**: (invoke-restart (find-restart (quote abort))) also works at level 1 but not reliably at nested levels.

**Documentation impact**: the skill's SBCL section currently shows (invoke-restart (find-restart (quote abort))) — this should be updated to recommend numbered restarts.

**Reproduction**:
1. muxxy --kind sbcl execute-command '(this-fn-is-undefined 1)' --timeout 15
2. muxxy --kind sbcl execute-command '(abort)' --timeout 10
→ prompt stays at '0]', (abort) did not exit debugger
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Daniel Jay Haskin
comments.text: Updated README and skill guidance to use numbered SBCL restarts; (abort) is explicitly documented as unreliable for leaving the debugger.

title: Bug: custom prompt regexes that match output prefixes silently eat output
description:
If a --prompt regex can match a prefix of an output line, muxxy treats that line as a prompt: strip_prompt empties it, the output filter drops it, and (for idle matching) the REPL may be considered idle while still working.

**Example**: custom prompt '^ *[0-9]+(\[[0-9]+\])?' (a plausible attempt at matching SBCL's nested debugger prompt) also matches bare numeric output lines like '1024' and '30'. Result: execute-command returns output: '' for commands whose output is numeric.

**Root cause**: prompt patterns are matched against ALL lines in the pane, including output lines, with no distinction between 'prompt lines' and 'output lines'. The built-in kinds happen to be carefully designed to avoid matching output, but there is no guardrail for custom regexes.

**Impact**: silent data loss in output; could also cause premature idle detection for slow commands whose intermediate output matches the pattern.

**Suggestion**: document the hazard, and/or validate that custom prompt regexes don't match numeric/bare lines; or only treat a line as a command boundary if it ALSO has non-whitespace after the prompt prefix (which is what idle_match does, but is_prompt_line/search does not).
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Daniel Jay Haskin
comments.text: Fixed in code/docs: prompt history matching and stripping now require line-prefix matches; custom --prompt regexes warn when matching ordinary output samples such as 1024; added regression tests.

title: Bug: default --max-lines 200 is too small for large outputs
description:
The default --max-lines of 200 is insufficient for commands that produce large output (e.g., asdf:load-system, asdf:test-system with test suites). The command echo + output scrolls beyond the 200-line capture window, so execute-command returns last_command: null and output: null even though the command succeeded.

**Impact**: users must remember to pass --max-lines 5000 (or higher) for any command that might produce significant output. This is a discoverability/usability issue.

**Reproduction**:
1. muxxy --kind sbcl execute-command '(asdf:load-system :com.djhaskin.dsolv)' --timeout 120
→ returns status: ok, last_command: null, output: null (test output was ~500+ lines)

**Suggestion**: either increase the default, or make it auto-adjust to capture the full command block.
close_reason: Default --max-lines raised from 200 to 5000 so large outputs (e.g. SBCL system loads, test suites) are captured without the user needing to pass --max-lines explicitly. Verified with 500+ line output capture: new default works, old 200 value reproduces the null/null bug. All 27 unit + 12 integration tests pass.

title: Bug: SBCL nested debugger prompt 0[2] not matched by sbcl kind
description:
When an error occurs inside the debugger (nested debugger level >= 2), SBCL shows the prompt as '0[2] ' (error number 0, debug level 2) instead of '0] '. The sbcl kind regex '^ *[0-9]+\] ?' requires ']' right after the digits and does not match '0[2]', so muxxy can never detect the REPL as ready: is-repl-ready returns false forever, execute-command times out.

**Fix**: change the numbered debugger prompt regex to '^ *[0-9]+(\[[0-9]+\]|\])' which matches both '0] ' and '0[2] ' without matching bare numeric output lines (e.g. '1024').

**Verified fix**: with custom prompt '^ *[0-9]+(\[[0-9]+\]|\])', is-repl-ready correctly detects 0[2], execute-command works inside the nested debugger, and numeric output is preserved. Also needs the top-level '^\* ' prompt in the same prompt set, or exiting the debugger times out (prompt style transition).

**Reproduction**:
1. muxxy --kind sbcl execute-command '(error "first")' --timeout 15
2. muxxy --kind sbcl execute-command '(error "nested")' --timeout 10
→ times out waiting for prompt; pane shows '0[2] '
close_reason: Closed

title: Bug: rlwrap/SBCL echo without prompt prefix breaks command boundary detection
description:
After multi-line input (via send-keys or execute-command with embedded newlines), rlwrap echoes the input lines WITHOUT the '* ' prompt prefix. muxxy's second_to_last_prompt_index then walks back past the un-prefixed input to the previous prompt-prefixed line, returning stale last_command and output.

**Root cause**: the muxxy prompt-based command extraction relies on echoed input lines having the prompt prefix, but rlwrap's echo is unreliable — some lines get the prefix, some don't.

**Impact**: execute-command returns wrong last_command; get-last-command returns stale data; subsequent commands compound the error.

**Reproduction**:
1. muxxy --kind sbcl send-keys $'(defun foo (n)\n  (* n n))\n'
2. sleep 3
3. muxxy --kind sbcl execute-command '(foo 9)' --timeout 10
→ last_command shows a previous command, output includes stale history

**To clarify**: I found this bug interesting, but I'm not entirely sure it's a bug in muxxy, rather than in clrepl's rlwrap config ('--only-cook', '--forget-matching'). The echo inconsistency is at the rlwrap layer. But muxxy relies on that echo being consistent, so it's a compatibility bug either way.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Daniel Jay Haskin
comments.text: Fixed execute-command recovery: when rlwrap omits a prompt prefix, the sent command is used to recover the current command/output boundary. get-last-command remains documented as inherently limited when no sent command is available.
